newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Menem loses lawsuit against journalist.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem loses lawsuit against journalist.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem on Tuesday lost a lawsuit he initated against a local journalist and was ordered to bear the costs of the trial.

Horacio Verbitsky wrote in an article that contrary to what Menem had said, Menem was never tortured during the several years he spent under arrest during the past military dictatorship and that he "cried like a sissy."

"The journalist fulfilled the duty imposed by his job when he said Menem was not telling the truth," judge Maria Garrigos de Libori said on live TV referring to Verbitsky, a widely known political researcher of lefstist newspaper Pagina/12.
"When saying he cried like a sissy" Verbitsky was not referring to the president's sexuality but rather to a "lack of courage," added the judge, who ordered Menem to pay the costs of the trial.
She also acquitted the editors of Pagina/12, who had been sued by Menem.
Under the dictatorship 15,000 people were killed or dissapeared according to official data but human rights groups put the number at 30,000.
The military leaders were sent to jail by Menem's predecessor, Raul Alfonsin, but Menem granted them a pardon along with leftist rebels soon after he took charge in 1989.
